evidence.note: Planning created dedicated tasks for BOTH surfaces, including an explicit console task (step 20) enumerating login/buckets/access-keys views, all required testids, in-app confirm and secret-once modal — shows deliberate reservation of effort for the UX half, not just the data plane.
Console was actually built: console.py, styles.css, app.js written. The neglected-half failure mode (stubbed/absent console) did not occur.

The entire verification arc — smoke tests, multipart, concurrency (30 clients), lifecycle, presigned/streaming — is data-plane only. No browser/DOM/testid check of the console ever occurs, so the UX surface never reaches a verified baseline and effort is not rebalanced by score weight.

reasoning: The agent consciously allocated effort to both surfaces during planning and build — the console was a named task and was fully written with awareness of its testid contract — so neither half was left unstarted (anchor 5). But there is no evidence of weight-aware sequencing to a verified baseline for both: the console was written once and never verified, while the entire iterative testing arc went to the data plane, falling short of the explicit, self-adjusting allocation described at anchor 8.
